title: OS binding: plug-in functions
description: Scripts in scope bound to specific operating systems through plug-in function calls: functions that do not exist on at least one OS (macOS / Windows / Linux / iOS). The verbatim vendor flags (binary, from the plug-in documentation) fold into the shared OS vocabulary through a curated map: the 'server' flag is a runtime statement and stays out of the OS profile (the Server x OS condition lives in the server compat member), 'iOS SDK' maps to the OS 'ios' with qualifier sdk-only - Claris iOS SDK apps, NOT FileMaker Go (Go supports no plug-ins). The os_profile uses the set-wide vocabulary (macos-only, windows-only, linux-only, ios-only, desktop-only, apple-only, mixed). Includes one-level custom-function wrappers (via_custom_function) and layout/field calculation usages (evidence_kind='layout'); the core metric counts scripts only. Inventory, not defects - findings are neutral properties, never errors.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: A plug-in function that exists only on certain operating systems binds every calling script to those systems - a hard 'does not exist elsewhere' (signal 'exclusive' on the OS sub-axis). This is the only structured OS signal in the platform model; Claris runtime environments stay OS-free.
rule.remediation: Nothing to fix. Use the inventory to know which scripts assume which OS; guard calls with Get(SystemPlatform) checks where a script must run cross-platform.
